Fields.DocComment: only counts newosproc0 stack in mstats; differs from MemStats.StackSys

Fields.Name: pause_ns
Fields.DocComment: circular buffer of recent gc pause lengths

Fields.Name: pause_end
Fields.DocComment: circular buffer of recent gc end times (nanoseconds since 1970)

Fields.Name: gc_cpu_fraction
Fields.DocComment: fraction of CPU time used by GC

Fields.Name: lastHeapInUse
Fields.DocComment: heapInUse at mark termination of the previous GC

nodes.Name: MemStats
nodes.DocComment: A MemStats records statistics about the memory allocator.

nodes.Name: ReadMemStats
nodes.DocComment:
ReadMemStats populates m with memory allocator statistics.

The returned memory allocator statistics are up to date as of the
call to ReadMemStats. This is in contrast with a heap profile,
which is a snapshot as of the most recently completed garbage
collection cycle.

nodes.Name: doubleCheckReadMemStats
nodes.DocComment:
doubleCheckReadMemStats controls a double-check mode for ReadMemStats that
ensures consistency between the values that ReadMemStats is using and the
runtime-internal stats.

nodes.Name: readmemstats_m
nodes.DocComment:
readmemstats_m populates stats for internal runtime values.

The world must be stopped.

nodes.Name: readGCStats
nodes.DocComment: go:linkname readGCStats runtime/debug.readGCStats

nodes.Name: readGCStats_m
nodes.DocComment:
readGCStats_m must be called on the system stack because it acquires the heap
lock. See mheap for details.

go:systemstack

nodes.Name: flushmcache
nodes.DocComment:
flushmcache flushes the mcache of allp[i].

The world must be stopped.

go:nowritebarrier

nodes.Name: flushallmcaches
nodes.DocComment:
flushallmcaches flushes the mcaches of all Ps.

The world must be stopped.

go:nowritebarrier

nodes.Name: sysMemStat
nodes.DocComment:
sysMemStat represents a global system statistic that is managed atomically.

This type must structurally be a uint64 so that mstats aligns with MemStats.

nodes.Name: load
nodes.DocComment:
load atomically reads the value of the stat.

Must be nosplit as it is called in runtime initialization, e.g. newosproc0.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: add
nodes.DocComment:
add atomically adds the sysMemStat by n.

Must be nosplit as it is called in runtime initialization, e.g. newosproc0.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: heapStatsDelta
nodes.DocComment:
heapStatsDelta contains deltas of various runtime memory statistics
that need to be updated together in order for them to be kept
consistent with one another.

Fields.Name: released
Fields.DocComment: byte delta of released memory generated

Fields.Name: inHeap
Fields.DocComment: byte delta of memory placed in the heap

Fields.Name: inStacks
Fields.DocComment: byte delta of memory reserved for stacks

Fields.Name: inWorkBufs
Fields.DocComment: byte delta of memory reserved for work bufs

Fields.Name: smallAllocCount
Fields.DocComment: number of allocs for small objects

Fields.Name: largeFreeCount
Fields.DocComment: number of frees for large objects (>maxSmallSize)

Fields.Name: smallFreeCount
Fields.DocComment: number of frees for small objects (<=maxSmallSize)

nodes.Name: merge
nodes.DocComment: merge adds in the deltas from b into a.

nodes.Name: consistentHeapStats
nodes.DocComment:
consistentHeapStats represents a set of various memory statistics
whose updates must be viewed completely to get a consistent
state of the world.

To write updates to memory stats use the acquire and release
methods. To obtain a consistent global snapshot of these statistics,
use read.

nodes.Name: acquire
nodes.DocComment:
acquire returns a heapStatsDelta to be updated. In effect,
it acquires the shard for writing. release must be called
as soon as the relevant deltas are updated.

The returned heapStatsDelta must be updated atomically.

The caller's P must not change between acquire and
release. This also means that the caller should not
acquire a P or release its P in between. A P also must
not acquire a given consistentHeapStats if it hasn't
yet released it.

nosplit because a stack growth in this function could
lead to a stack allocation that could reenter the
function.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: release
nodes.DocComment:
release indicates that the writer is done modifying
the delta. The value returned by the corresponding
acquire must no longer be accessed or modified after
release is called.

The caller's P must not change between acquire and
release. This also means that the caller should not
acquire a P or release its P in between.

nosplit because a stack growth in this function could
lead to a stack allocation that causes another acquire
before this operation has completed.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: unsafeRead
nodes.DocComment:
unsafeRead aggregates the delta for this shard into out.

Unsafe because it does so without any synchronization. The
world must be stopped.

nodes.Name: unsafeClear
nodes.DocComment:
unsafeClear clears the shard.

Unsafe because the world must be stopped and values should
be donated elsewhere before clearing.

nodes.Name: read
nodes.DocComment:
read takes a globally consistent snapshot of m
and puts the aggregated value in out. Even though out is a
heapStatsDelta, the resulting values should be complete and
valid statistic values.

Not safe to call concurrently. The world must be stopped
or metricsSema must be held.

Fields.Name: GCPauseTime
Fields.DocComment: GC pauses (all GOMAXPROCS, even if just 1 is running)

Fields.Name: UserTime
Fields.DocComment: Time Ps spent in _Prunning that's not any of the above.

nodes.Name: accumulateGCPauseTime
nodes.DocComment:
accumulateGCPauseTime add dt*stwProcs to the GC CPU pause time stats. dt should be
the actual time spent paused, for orthogonality. maxProcs should be GOMAXPROCS,
not work.stwprocs, since this number must be comparable to a total time computed
from GOMAXPROCS.

nodes.Name: accumulate
nodes.DocComment:
accumulate takes a cpuStats and adds in the current state of all GC CPU
counters.

gcMarkPhase indicates that we're in the mark phase and that certain counter
values should be used.
